newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices inch higher on weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices inch higher on weather.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly inched higher Wednesday in moderate trade, with record power demand along the East Coast still underpinning the complex, industry sources said.

"Near-term, resid feels pretty good. All the utilities are burning with this heat, and even though they're sitting on pretty good stocks, they're going to have to replace the barrels eventually," said one East Coast trader, noting some grades of resid were now competitive with gas after this week's rally in city gate gas prices.
While temperatures in the East are forecast to remain above-normal for most of the week, more seasonal weather is expected for the weekend and next week.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent edged up a quarter to about the $17 a barrel area, with August one percent paper up 10-15 cents to $16.50-75 despite little movement in crude. September paper was quoted slightly higher at $16.20-35, while Q4 was pegged at $16.40-65.
A New York utility tendered for two cargoes of one percent for delivery by 7/30-8/4 and 8/6-10. Bids are due Thursday.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour also inched higher, with buyers and sellers now stradling $18. Traders said reports of some West African material due later this month helped slow gains.
High sulphurs in New York also were modestly higher, with 2.2 percent now talked around $15.25.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were steady to higher, with one percent still in the low-$16s, while three percent firmed a quarter to $14.50-75.
A trader said 50,000 barrels of USG three percent for July 20-22 delivery sold at $14.50.

New York city gate swing gas firmed a few cents Wednesday to the mid-to-high $2.50s/mmBtu, or $16.19 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, gained three cents to $2.23/mmBtu, or $14.05 a barrel.
